title: Learn This Skill If You Want To Win In The Next 2-3 Years

sentences.en: Nobody knows what skill to learn right now.
sentences.zh: 现在没人知道该学什么技能。

sentences.en: Do you learn AI?
sentences.zh: 学 AI 吗？

sentences.en: Do you learn coding? Do you learn marketing?
sentences.zh: 学编程？学营销？

sentences.en: Am I wasting my time if I go to school while everyone else is vibe coding?
sentences.zh: 别人都在 vibe coding，我去上学是不是在浪费时间？

sentences.en: Apps they'll never get traction on.
sentences.zh: 做那些永远不会有用户的 App。

sentences.en: Do I start a YouTube channel?
sentences.zh: 我要不要开个 YouTube 频道？

sentences.en: What about a Substack?
sentences.zh: Substack 怎么样？

sentences.en: Should I even try getting a job?
sentences.zh: 我甚至该不该试着找份工作？

sentences.en: Or should I build my own thing?
sentences.zh: 还是应该自己搞点东西？

sentences.en: There is so much opportunity right now, and I'm sure you've heard that a billion times before.
sentences.zh: 现在机会太多了，我敢肯定你听过无数遍了。

sentences.en: But since there is so much opportunity, it just paralyzes more people than ever into not doing anything because you feel like if you start learning one thing, it'll just become irrelevant in 1 to 2 years.
sentences.zh: 但正因为机会太多，反而让更多人陷入瘫痪，什么都不做，因为你总觉得一旦开始学某个东西，一两年后它就过时了。

sentences.en: However, there is one skill that will never go out of style.
sentences.zh: 然而，有一项技能永远不会过时。

sentences.en: It is a meta skill and if you learn it, it simply increases the power of every other skill that you learn, and it allows you to learn those skills much faster.
sentences.zh: 它是一项元技能，一旦你学会它，它会直接增强你学到的其他所有技能的力量，并且让你学那些技能的速度快得多。

sentences.en: And that skill is called human nature.
sentences.zh: 这项技能叫做人性。

sentences.en: Because if you understand how the mind works, what makes it tick, what makes it pay attention, what makes it take action, then you can really make any business successful.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你理解心智如何运作，什么让它运转，什么让它产生注意力，什么让它采取行动，那你几乎可以让任何生意成功。

sentences.en: You can work your way into new opportunities.
sentences.zh: 你可以靠它进入新的机会。

sentences.en: You can make friends and influence people.
sentences.zh: 你可以交到朋友、影响他人。

sentences.en: You can navigate through life with elegance and grace because you are no longer a slave to your mind, but a master of it and a master of others.
sentences.zh: 你可以优雅从容地驾驭人生，因为你不再是你心智的奴隶，而是它的主人，也是他人的主人。

sentences.en: And if you want to build your own thing, how else are you going to succeed outside of a job?
sentences.zh: 如果你想自己搞点东西，不靠工作，你还能怎么成功？

sentences.en: When humans are the ones with the money, the resources, the opportunities that are going to support you?
sentences.zh: 当掌握金钱、资源、机会、能支持你的是人？

sentences.en: How else are you going to get paid?
sentences.zh: 你还能怎么获得报酬？

sentences.en: If another human with money doesn't see you as valuable enough to pay?
sentences.zh: 如果一个有钱的人不觉得你足够有价值，他会付你钱吗？

sentences.en: And even if your goal is to get a job and not do your own thing.
sentences.zh: 即使你的目标是找份工作，而不是自己搞事。

sentences.en: How are you going to get your dream job if you don't position yourself as valuable to the employer?
sentences.zh: 如果你不把自己定位成对雇主有价值的人，你怎么拿到梦想的工作？

sentences.en: But the question is, how do you learn something as intangible as human nature?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，人性这么无形的东西，你怎么学？

sentences.en: So in this video, that's what I hope to provide.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个视频里，这就是我想提供的。

sentences.en: I hope to provide the steps and principles that you can apply today that will give you a competitive advantage against everyone else who is racing to succeed as fast as possible, because they think AI will somehow save them from their lack of experience.
sentences.zh: 我想提供你今天就能应用的步骤和原则，让你获得竞争优势，胜过所有那些拼命追求快速成功的人，因为他们以为 AI 会莫名其妙地拯救他们缺乏经验的短板。

sentences.en: So we're going to start with dissecting the anatomy of human nature and how to exploit it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们先从解剖人性的结构以及如何利用它开始。

sentences.en: Now, you may not like the word exploit here, but we'll get to that and what it means to do this unethically or ethically.
sentences.zh: 你可能不喜欢"利用"这个词，但我们后面会讲到，以及不道德地或道德地做这件事意味着什么。

sentences.en: Now there are eight human desires.
sentences.zh: 人有八种欲望。

sentences.en: There's survival, life enjoyment, social acceptance, sexual companionship, freedom from fear, comfort and clarity, perceived status and safety of tribe.
sentences.zh: 生存、享受生活、社会接纳、性伴侣、免于恐惧、舒适与清晰、感知地位、族群安全。

sentences.en: We're going to condense all of these into what I call the three tensions.
sentences.zh: 我们要把这些浓缩成我所说的三种张力。

sentences.en: These are the three psychological tensions that if you know how to hit, you can get people to pay attention and you can position yourself or your work or your writing, or you're speaking or your social media posts or your landing pages or products as valuable.
sentences.zh: 这三种心理张力，如果你知道如何击中，你就能抓住人们的注意力，把自己、你的作品、你的写作、你的演讲、你的社交媒体帖子、你的落地页或产品定位成有价值的东西。

sentences.en: This is a meta skill. It applies to everything.
sentences.zh: 这是一项元技能。它适用于一切。

sentences.en: And then after that, we're going to actually make that actionable with the five psychological levers that you can actually pull and apply to your speaking, your writing, everything that you do on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 然后在那之后，我们会用五个你可以实际运用的心理杠杆，让这些东西变得可操作，你可以把它们用在你的演讲、写作、你每天做的每一件事上。

sentences.en: And if you practice those five things, you'll be unstoppable.
sentences.zh: 如果你练习这五件事，你将势不可挡。

sentences.en: As hyperbolic as that sounds.
sentences.zh: 不管这听起来有多夸张。

sentences.en: Now, the mind is a story engine.
sentences.zh: 现在，记住，大脑是一个故事引擎。

sentences.en: That's what humans can't help but pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 这是人类无法不去关注的东西。

sentences.en: And that's what separates us from robots.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们区别于机器人的地方。

sentences.en: Because robots are useful for utility, because nobody would care.
sentences.zh: 因为机器人是用来解决实用性的，没人会关心那个。

sentences.en: Aside from the DMV workers, if the DMV was completely automated and made efficient, who in their right mind looks forward to standing in a long line for hours just to get a new picture for your driver's license?
sentences.zh: 除了DMV的工作人员，如果DMV完全自动化、变得高效，哪个正常人会期待排几个小时的队，就为了换一张驾照照片？

sentences.en: It just doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 这根本说不通。

sentences.en: People want to get rid of this, and it's the same with fast food or writing in an Uber or a taxi.
sentences.zh: 人们想摆脱这些，快餐也一样，叫Uber或出租车也一样。

sentences.en: Nobody likes when the cashier gets your order wrong.
sentences.zh: 没人喜欢收银员弄错你的订单。

sentences.en: Nobody likes riding in a dirty back seat while someone you don't know asked about your day simply because they want you to tip them more money.
sentences.zh: 没人喜欢坐在脏兮兮的后座，听一个陌生人问你今天过得怎么样，只因为他想让你多给点小费。

sentences.en: So let the robot solve utility.
sentences.zh: 所以，让机器人去解决实用性问题。

sentences.en: That way humans can abstract out to meaning, purpose, and narrative.
sentences.zh: 这样人类就可以抽身出来，去关注意义、目的和叙事。

sentences.en: Humans love stakes, or chess gets tight when their team is about to lose in the final inning of a baseball game.
sentences.zh: 人类热爱悬念，热爱自己支持的球队在棒球比赛最后一局快要输掉时的紧张感。

sentences.en: Humans love novelty.
sentences.zh: 人类热爱新奇。

sentences.en: We travel across the world to dine in a five star restaurant, so Mastering human nature is about mastering story, storytelling, narrative.
sentences.zh: 我们飞越半个地球，只为了在一家五星级餐厅吃一顿饭。所以，掌握人性就是掌握故事、讲故事、叙事。

sentences.en: And I'm not talking about writing a novel.
sentences.zh: 我说的不是写小说。

sentences.en: I'm talking about like, the structure of reality in a sense.
sentences.zh: 我说的是，某种意义上，现实的底层结构。

sentences.en: So I'm not going to teach you how to write a short story.
sentences.zh: 所以我不是要教你写短篇小说。

sentences.en: I'm going to teach you the principles of value creation, to get people to pay attention, to position what you have to offer as valuable, and to get them to take action on it.
sentences.zh: 我要教你的是价值创造的原则，如何抓住别人的注意力，如何把你提供的东西定位成有价值的，以及如何让他们为此采取行动。

sentences.en: Be that to pay you to change their own behavior or to just get what you want, which will go over.
sentences.zh: 无论是让他们付钱给你来改变他们自己的行为，还是让你得到你想要的，这些我们都会讲到。

sentences.en: Now, if you understand these principles that we're going to go over, you will write better, speak better, create better products, attract more customers, make more friends, and understand how to create value for others, thus increasing the value of yourself.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你理解了我们将要讲的这些原则，你会写得更好、讲得更好、做出更好的产品、吸引更多客户、交到更多朋友，并且理解如何为他人创造价值，从而提升你自己的价值。

sentences.en: So in essence, I'm teaching you marketing, sales and how to influence people all in one go, and I genuinely don't think you'll understand the importance of this until you actually implement it, which most people won't. I made a video,
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，我在一次性教你营销、销售和如何影响他人，而且我真的认为，在你真正去实践之前，你不会理解这有多重要，而大多数人不会去实践。我做过一个视频，

sentences.en: I think like three years ago on the same topic.
sentences.zh: 大概是三年前，同一个主题。

sentences.en: And for the people that actually understand this and what I'm saying here and see the patterns across all the different industries, it is completely life changing.
sentences.zh: 对于那些真正理解这个、理解我在这里说的东西、并且能在不同行业里看到这些模式的人，这完全是改变人生的。

sentences.en: It is completely different frame from how you operate within the world.
sentences.zh: 这完全是一个不同的、你在这个世界上运作的框架。

sentences.en: And I'm genuinely convinced that this is the frame that most successful people have, and unsuccessful people simply just can't see through it.
sentences.zh: 而且我真的确信，这就是大多数成功人士拥有的框架，而不成功的人就是看不透它。

sentences.en: So the mind has three pressure points, and if you press any one of them, attention them.
sentences.zh: 所以，大脑有三个压力点，只要你按下其中任何一个，注意力就来了。

sentences.en: Giving you attention is almost involuntary.
sentences.zh: 给你注意力几乎是下意识的。

sentences.en: That is, if you're speaking to a person who is prone to that specific tension or pressure point.
sentences.zh: 前提是，你说话的对象正好对那种特定的紧张感或压力点敏感。

sentences.en: And if you press all three of them, you have a grip on someone that logic alone can't break.
sentences.zh: 如果你三个压力点同时按下，你对一个人的掌控力，是单靠逻辑无法打破的。

sentences.en: So I want you to keep these three tensions in mind whenever you interact with someone, or go to write something or anything where you're interacting with another person.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你，无论何时与人互动、去写东西、或者做任何需要跟另一个人打交道的事情时，都把这三个紧张感记在心里。

sentences.en: Writing on social media is interacting with a bunch of people at once.
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体上写作，就是一次性跟一大群人互动。

sentences.en: Just hold it in your mind until it sticks in there.
sentences.zh: 把它牢牢刻在脑子里，直到它扎根。

sentences.en: Now, the first tension is the survival tension because the mind is a story engine, but it's also a set of survival strategies.
sentences.zh: 第一种张力是生存张力，因为大脑不仅是一个故事引擎，也是一套生存策略。

sentences.en: We're in a constant subconscious threat detection mode because we still have the same wiring as our hunter gatherer ancestors.
sentences.zh: 我们始终处于一种潜意识的威胁检测模式，因为我们和狩猎采集祖先的神经回路是一样的。

sentences.en: We don't want to die, obviously, so we desire safety and solutions to problems.
sentences.zh: 我们显然不想死，所以我们渴望安全，渴望问题的解决方案。

sentences.en: And if you can make someone aware of a problem, then provide a solution.
sentences.zh: 如果你能让一个人意识到一个问题，然后提供一个解决方案。

sentences.en: That's sales in a nutshell and storytelling in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 这就是销售的本质，也是讲故事的本质。

sentences.en: So when I personally talk about storytelling again, I'm not talking about writing a novel.
sentences.zh: 所以当我个人谈论讲故事时，我并不是在说写小说。

sentences.en: I'm talking about problem solution.
sentences.zh: 我说的是问题与解决方案。

sentences.en: That's what.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: And in between the transformation in between problem transformation solution.
sentences.zh: 以及从问题到解决方案之间的转变过程。

sentences.en: But the thing with the survival tension is that safety isn't just life or death situations.
sentences.zh: 但生存张力的关键在于，安全并不仅仅关乎生死。

sentences.en: It can be a very small problem that is amplified into a big problem.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一个很小的、被放大成严重问题的事情。

sentences.en: And these problems can be financial or social or even just a missed opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这些问题可以是财务上的、社交上的，甚至只是一个错失的机会。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: FOMO because that gives you better chances that survival.
sentences.zh: FOMO，因为它能给你更好的生存机会。

sentences.en: Your mind is constantly looking for something that gives them a better chance at survival.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑会不断寻找任何能提高生存概率的东西。

sentences.en: And in today's world, that doesn't mean like necessarily better shelter or better home.
sentences.zh: 在今天的世界，这未必意味着更好的住所或更好的房子。

sentences.en: It means better skills, better knowledge.
sentences.zh: 它意味着更好的技能、更好的知识。

sentences.en: So you can stay on top of, let's say, AI.
sentences.zh: 这样你才能跟上，比如说，AI 的发展。

sentences.en: If someone on Instagram is like, oh, I have the latest Claude skill that you can download, and it does this, this and this.
sentences.zh: 如果 Instagram 上有个人说，嘿，我有最新的 Claude 使用技巧可以下载，它能做到这个、这个还有这个。

sentences.en: Then you feel the sense of missed opportunity because you don't use Claude the same way and you feel like you need to learn that.
sentences.zh: 你就会感到一种错失机会的焦虑，因为你没有用同样的方式使用 Claude，你觉得自己必须学会那个。

sentences.en: And the thing there is that it could genuinely be helpful, but you as a person, to protect your own mind from being manipulated is you have to ruthlessly maintain your priorities and your values and your goals, because that Claude skill may not have anything to do with your priorities or goals, and you may get sucked in and distracted.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，那个技巧可能真的有用，但你作为一个人，要保护自己的大脑不被操控，就必须无情地守住你的优先级、你的价值观和你的目标，因为那个 Claude 技巧可能跟你的优先级或目标毫无关系，而你可能会被吸进去、被带偏。

sentences.en: That's the definition of distraction.
sentences.zh: 这就是分心的定义。

sentences.en: So a few examples of this well worded examples of the survival tension illustrated as a problem or something that you would say, I guess is one, you wake up at 30 and realize you've been living on autopilot, and the gap between who you are and who you want to be is so large that change feels impossible.
sentences.zh: 举几个例子，一些措辞精炼的、把生存张力表现为问题的例子，或者说你会说出口的话：第一，你三十岁醒来，发现自己一直活在自动驾驶模式里，现在的你和你想成为的你之间的鸿沟如此巨大，以至于改变感觉根本不可能。

sentences.en: Two you spend a decade building someone else's dreams just to find that they don't care about you at all.
sentences.zh: 第二，你花了十年时间构建别人的梦想，最后发现他们根本不在乎你。

sentences.en: Three there are people dumber than you, making ten times more than you because they don't think about the risk.
sentences.zh: 第三，有些比你笨的人，赚的是你的十倍，因为他们根本不考虑风险。

sentences.en: And as you may be able to tell, I've written those before as social posts and they grab attention because of this exact tension.
sentences.zh: 你可能看得出来，这些我都写成过社交媒体帖子，它们之所以能抓住注意力，正是因为这种张力。

sentences.en: Now, a quick aside and a quick self-promotion.
sentences.zh: 现在，稍微岔开一下，做个快速的自我推广。

sentences.en: If you want to build your personal brand in 30 days and learn the AI skills that you actually need, the next content bootcamp starts in just a few days, and this will teach you everything that you need to know about personal branding content, how to write, how to generate compelling ideas that actually allow you to grow and get clients, or just new opportunities, even new jobs.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在 30 天内建立你的个人品牌，并学会你真正需要的 AI 技能，下一期内容训练营几天后就要开始了，它会教你关于个人品牌内容的一切，如何写作，如何生成真正能让你成长、获得客户、或者新机会甚至新工作的有吸引力的想法。

sentences.en: So if you want to learn a skill that compounds for the rest of your career, consider enrolling with the link in the description.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想学一个能在你整个职业生涯中持续复利的技能，考虑用描述里的链接报名。

sentences.en: Now, the second tension is the identity tension.
sentences.zh: 现在，第二种张力是身份张力。

sentences.en: And this comes after survival because it's deeply intertwined with survival, because survival goes much deeper than physical survival.
sentences.zh: 它出现在生存之后，因为它与生存深度交织，因为生存远不止肉体生存。

sentences.en: Animals try to reproduce the information in their genes through physical reproduction.
sentences.zh: 动物试图通过肉体繁殖来复制它们基因中的信息。

sentences.en: Humans also do that, but we also try to reproduce the information in our consciousness through ideology, speaking, socialization.
sentences.zh: 人类也这么做，但我们也试图通过意识形态、言说、社交来复制我们意识中的信息。

sentences.en: That's all we're doing. It's just all survival.
sentences.zh: 我们做的所有事，归根结底都是生存。

sentences.en: This is why you feel threatened when someone threatens your identity, when they say, oh, your sports team sucks and you're too identified with the sports team.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当有人威胁到你的身份认同时，你会感到被冒犯——比如他们说，哦，你支持的球队烂透了，而你又过度认同那支球队。

sentences.en: And when they lose, you're on the verge of fighting someone.
sentences.zh: 球队一输，你就差点要跟人干架。

sentences.en: Or you do get in a bar fight because of it.
sentences.zh: 或者你真的因此在酒吧打了起来。

sentences.en: Or when someone says something bad about being a Republican or a Democrat or a Christian or an atheist or anything else, any ideology, any set of concepts that you hold as a part of yourself in your little mind, you get threatened by that, and you feel the response as if someone's holding a knife to your throat, even though they're not.
sentences.zh: 又或者，当有人说共和党、民主党、基督徒、无神论者或任何其他东西的坏话——任何被你这个小脑袋当成自我一部分的意识形态、任何概念集合——你都会感到威胁，你的反应就像有人拿刀抵着你的喉咙，尽管并没有。

sentences.en: Humans desire a tribe because it helps with survival, and you identify with that tribe.
sentences.zh: 人类渴望部落，因为这有助于生存，而你认同那个部落。

sentences.en: Humans desire status.
sentences.zh: 人类渴望地位。

sentences.en: They want belonging because again, in your home, if you rebel against your parents, they're going to kick you out potentially, if they're not open minded.
sentences.zh: 他们想要归属感，同样是因为，在家里如果你反抗父母，他们可能会把你赶出去——如果他们思想不够开明的话。

sentences.en: So you have to conform to their values and beliefs and their rules.
sentences.zh: 所以你不得不顺从他们的价值观、信念和规则。

sentences.en: This is also why you choose to be anti-air or pro AI, which is the new religion, and you argue into oblivion about it all day on social media with nothing to show for it.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么你选择成为反AI派或挺AI派——这已经成了新宗教——然后整天在社交媒体上争论到天荒地老，却拿不出任何成果。

sentences.en: You get nowhere.
sentences.zh: 你哪儿也到不了。

sentences.en: You can regurgitate how AI is rotting your brain, or you can test that theory against reality and actually educate yourself on it.
sentences.zh: 你可以复述AI如何腐蚀你的大脑，也可以拿这个理论去跟现实碰撞，真正去学习了解它。

sentences.en: But that's not the point of this.
sentences.zh: 但这不是重点。

sentences.en: That's a way to make yourself unsuspecting to people targeting your identity tension.
sentences.zh: 那是一种让你对瞄准你身份张力的人毫无防备的方式。

sentences.en: Because every time you argue about the anti AI stuff or pro AI stuff, you are a slave to someone else's ideals and you do not seek truth, you seek hype and you have not created your own mind.
sentences.zh: 因为每次你争论反AI或挺AI的东西，你都是在做别人理想的奴隶，你不是在寻求真相，你是在追逐热度，你还没有创造出自己的头脑。

sentences.en: So that's the identity tension and we'll learn how to target it.
sentences.zh: 这就是身份张力，我们会学习如何瞄准它。

sentences.en: We're just going over what it is for now.
sentences.zh: 现在只是先讲清楚它是什么。

sentences.en: But the third tension is the progress tension.
sentences.zh: 第三种张力是进步张力。

sentences.en: So there's survival identity progress.
sentences.zh: 所以是生存、身份、进步。

sentences.en: And they each build on top of each other.
sentences.zh: 它们一层层叠加。

sentences.en: People kind of evolve through the stages.
sentences.zh: 人们大致会经历这些阶段来进化。

sentences.en: And by now you may be able to see the pattern which is Maslow's hierarchy, the stages of ego development, spiral dynamics, developmental psychology.
sentences.zh: 到现在你可能已经看出了模式——马斯洛需求层次、自我发展阶段、螺旋动力学、发展心理学。

sentences.en: In general, people at different levels of mind have different things that tap into their psychology and make them pay attention because they see it as important.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，不同心智层次的人，有不同的事物能触动他们的心理、让他们集中注意力，因为他们认为那些东西很重要。

sentences.en: So first, people need safety and comfort.
sentences.zh: 所以，第一，人们需要安全和舒适。

sentences.en: Second, they need belonging and status.
sentences.zh: 第二，他们需要归属感和地位。

sentences.en: And once they solve those things, which preferably you're helping them do because you're a value creator, you're not a manipulator.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们解决了这些——最好是在你的帮助下，因为你是一个价值创造者，而不是操纵者。

sentences.en: You're not exploiting human nature to be unethical and just make a bunch of money.
sentences.zh: 你不是在利用人性去做不道德的事、只为了赚一大笔钱。

sentences.en: You're exploiting it, so to say, so you can help people rise through these stages.
sentences.zh: 你是在利用它，可以这么说，来帮助人们穿越这些阶段。

sentences.en: That's the ethical and meaningful version of this.
sentences.zh: 这才是这件事合乎道德、有意义的方式。

sentences.en: And once they go through those first two stages, third, they crave deeper meaning, purpose and experience.
sentences.zh: 当他们走过了前两个阶段，第三，他们会渴望更深层的意义、目的和体验。

sentences.en: And the complex thing about humans is that you can desire any of these at different times, right?
sentences.zh: 而人类复杂的地方在于，你可以在不同时间渴望其中任何一种，对吧？

sentences.en: AI can't just pin down exactly where you are.
sentences.zh: AI没法精确锁定你具体在哪个位置。

sentences.en: That's why it's unique.
sentences.zh: 这就是它独特的地方。

sentences.en: That's why it's a difficult skill to learn in practice, because you're essentially able to read people's minds when you get it right.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它在实践中是一门难学的技能，因为当你做对了，你本质上是在读心。

sentences.en: But people can desire these at any time.
sentences.zh: 但人在任何时候都可能渴望这些东西。

sentences.en: You can desire meaning and purpose, but if you're in a very stressful situation in your life or you lose a lot of money at one time, then you're going to regress down to the survival stage and survival tension is going to hit you a lot harder, and you're going to be a lot more susceptible to people trying to exploit you.
sentences.zh: 你可能渴望意义和目的，但如果你正处在生活压力极大的阶段，或者一次性亏了很多钱，你就会退回到生存阶段，生存焦虑会猛烈冲击你，你也更容易被想利用你的人趁虚而入。

sentences.en: And for creators specifically, or personal brands or people who are trying to do their own work online, or the writers or the speakers or the writers or the speakers, the problem that I see is that people try to speak too much to the meaning and purpose crowd, without understanding that 90% to 95% of people are not only beginners, but in the survival and identity stages, you have to work them up the ladder.
sentences.zh: 具体到创作者、个人品牌，或者那些在网上做自己事业的人，写作者、演讲者，我看到的问题是，人们太想对着追求意义和目的的人群说话了，却没意识到 90% 到 95% 的人不仅是新手，还卡在生存和身份认同这两个阶段，你得一步步把他们往上带。

sentences.en: If you want your content to be seen, then usually your topics revolve around the survival tension and the identity tension, but then your products and your lead magnets and deeper in your funnel.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让自己的内容被看到，那你的话题通常要围绕生存焦虑和身份焦虑展开，而你的产品、引流磁石和漏斗更深层的东西，则另当别论。

sentences.en: If you're a value creator, so to say, and not just an influencer trying to sell a weird product, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 前提是你是一个价值创造者，而不是那种只想卖奇怪产品的网红，我不确定。

sentences.en: But you have to help them solve their lower level problems first, so that then you can help them with where you're experienced, in which is the meaning, the purpose, the spirituality, the fulfillment, all of that fun stuff, the deep philosophy.
sentences.zh: 你必须先帮他们解决底层问题，然后才能用你擅长的东西去帮他们——也就是意义、目的、灵性、满足感，所有这些有趣的东西，那些深刻的哲学。

sentences.en: And this all sounds great, but what do you actually do with this information?
sentences.zh: 这些听起来都不错，但你到底该怎么用这些信息？

sentences.en: How does it actually make you a better writer or speaker or businessman, or husband or wife, or just person, valuable person in general?
sentences.zh: 它到底怎么让你成为一个更好的写作者、演讲者、商人、丈夫、妻子，或者一个更有价值的人？

sentences.en: How do you practice this skill?
sentences.zh: 你怎么练习这个技能？

sentences.en: So now we're going to learn how to pull psychological levers to get what you want.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来学学，怎么拉动心理杠杆来得到你想要的。

sentences.en: And I want to start with just a quote that I love.
sentences.zh: 我想先引用一句我很喜欢的话。

sentences.en: I honestly pulled this from one of my previous newsletters.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这是我从自己之前一期 newsletter 里翻出来的。

sentences.en: I don't know if I wrote it or if someone else did, so I hope that I'm not just stealing someone's quote here, but the modern information environment is breaking our ability to think, and most people don't even notice.
sentences.zh: 我不确定是我写的还是别人写的，希望我不是在偷别人的话，但它是这么说的：现代信息环境正在摧毁我们的思考能力，而大多数人甚至毫无察觉。

sentences.en: Essays might be one of the last forms of content that actually develops your capacity to make sense of reality.
sentences.zh: 文章可能是最后几种能真正培养你理解现实能力的内容形式之一。

sentences.en: And I say this because you can read all the books on persuasion.
sentences.zh: 我这么说是因为，你可以读完所有关于说服的书。

sentences.en: You can study psychology and behavior textbooks.
sentences.zh: 你可以啃完心理学和行为学的教科书。

sentences.en: You can think you know a lot about why humans think and act the way they do.
sentences.zh: 你可以以为自己很懂人类为什么这么想、这么做。

sentences.en: But if you have not tested that knowledge against reality, then you do not know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有把这些知识拿到现实中去检验，那你根本不知道自己在说什么。

sentences.en: You need feedback.
sentences.zh: 你需要反馈。

sentences.en: You need to put something out into the world and see how people respond.
sentences.zh: 你需要把东西放到世界上，看看人们怎么回应。

sentences.en: You need to write. You need to speak.
sentences.zh: 你需要写作。你需要演讲。

sentences.en: You need to create a product and sell it.
sentences.zh: 你需要做出一个产品并把它卖掉。

sentences.en: Entrepreneurship equals self-improvement because the market and reality become your harsh mentor.
sentences.zh: 创业等于自我提升，因为市场和现实会变成你最严厉的导师。

sentences.en: This is why I recommend writing so much, because not only is writing clear thinking, you have to refine and clarify your thinking as you write it on the page.
sentences.zh: 这就是我为什么这么推崇写作，因为写作不仅是清晰的思考，你在纸上写下来的时候，必须不断打磨和澄清自己的想法。

sentences.en: But there's a dual mechanism.
sentences.zh: 但它还有一个双重机制。

sentences.en: When you post it, you get direct feedback as to how valuable it was, and in order for it to be valuable, it has to be attention grabbing and persuasive.
sentences.zh: 当你把它发出去，你会直接收到关于它有多大价值的反馈，而它要有价值，就必须能抓住注意力、有说服力。

sentences.en: You have to practice and refine the skill of human nature.
sentences.zh: 你必须练习和打磨人性这门技能。

sentences.en: So for now, understand that when I say you're pulling psychological levers or you're exploiting human nature, what I'm really saying is that you need to learn how to persuade, and persuasion is only as unethical as the person that wields the tool.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你要理解，当我说你在拉动心理杠杆或利用人性时，我真正的意思是，你需要学会说服，而说服这个工具是否道德，只取决于使用它的人。

sentences.en: It's the same with any other tool.
sentences.zh: 这和任何其他工具一样。

sentences.en: A tool like money or AI is neutral until it's put in the hands of the stupid, or the smart, or the unethical or the ethical.
sentences.zh: 像金钱或 AI 这样的工具，在落到蠢人、聪明人、不道德的人或有道德的人手里之前，都是中性的。

sentences.en: So someone who resides at a lower level of mind in survival mode, and all they can see is what is going to allow them to pay the bills this month.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个心智处在较低层次、活在生存模式里的人，眼里只能看到什么能让他付清这个月的账单。

sentences.en: They're going to do anything to make that happen, and they will inevitably use persuasion in unethical ways, since their sole priority is money rather than meaning or truth.
sentences.zh: 他会不惜一切代价去达成这个目标，并且不可避免地会以不道德的方式使用说服，因为他唯一看重的是钱，而不是意义或真相。

sentences.en: Because they don't feel comfortable financially, they will manipulate and scheme to acquire the money until those values fundamentally shift.
sentences.zh: 因为他在财务上没有安全感，他会操纵和算计来获取金钱，直到这些价值观从根本上发生转变。

sentences.en: So in my eyes, it's very important that you develop yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，发展你自己是非常重要的一件事。

sentences.en: You pursue personal development and truth so you can reach this higher level of mind.
sentences.zh: 你追求个人成长和真理，是为了达到这个更高层次的心智。

sentences.en: And I don't say that to say that the lower level of mind is bad.
sentences.zh: 我这么说，不是说低层次的心智就不好。

sentences.en: Most people just don't have control over it.
sentences.zh: 只是大多数人无法掌控它。

sentences.en: I think that is a great fundamental thing to pursue in your life, so that you have a more positive impact on your customers or your readers or whoever it may be.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是你人生中一个很值得追求的基本功，这样你就能对你的客户、读者或任何人产生更正面的影响。

sentences.en: So with that said, know where you stand, right?
sentences.zh: 所以说到这里，先搞清楚你处在什么位置，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm not here to tell you how to use persuasion.
sentences.zh: 我不是来教你怎么用说服术的。

sentences.en: That's you're going to use it however you plan to use it.
sentences.zh: 那是你自己的事，你想怎么用就怎么用。

sentences.en: Now, there are five psychological levers that pull one or more of the three tensions we just discussed.
sentences.zh: 好，现在有五个心理杠杆，它们能拉动我们刚聊过的三种张力中的一种或多种。

sentences.en: So you create tension first.
sentences.zh: 所以你先制造张力。

sentences.en: This is what gets people to pay attention when you write, speak, post or sell.
sentences.zh: 这就是你写东西、说话、发帖或卖东西时，抓住别人注意力的方法。

sentences.en: And then you offer a solution that preferably changes behavior in a positive way.
sentences.zh: 然后你提供一个解决方案，最好是以积极的方式改变行为。

sentences.en: Now the first lever psychological lever is name the threat, which aligns with the survival tension.
sentences.zh: 第一个心理杠杆是“点明威胁”，这对应的是生存张力。

sentences.en: Because before anyone cares about a solution like your video or product, etc., they need to be aware of the problem.
sentences.zh: 因为在任何人关心一个解决方案之前，比如你的视频或产品，他们得先意识到问题的存在。

sentences.en: And there are five levels of awareness and these are from Eugene Schwartz.
sentences.zh: 这里有五个意识层级，来自 Eugene Schwartz。

sentences.en: The first level is unaware, so they don't know they have a problem and you make them aware of it by just naming it.
sentences.zh: 第一级是“无意识”，他们不知道自己有问题，你通过直接点明问题，让他们意识到。

sentences.en: Level two is problem aware so they know there's a problem but don't know a solution exists.
sentences.zh: 第二级是“问题意识”，他们知道有问题，但不知道有解决方案。

sentences.en: So you just name the solution here.
sentences.zh: 所以你在这里直接点明解决方案。

sentences.en: Level three is solution aware.
sentences.zh: 第三级是“方案意识”。

sentences.en: So they know the solution exists, but they're comparing options and don't know about your unique solution.
sentences.zh: 他们知道有解决方案，但正在比较不同选项，还不知道你独特的方案。

sentences.en: And level four is product aware.
sentences.zh: 第四级是“产品意识”。

sentences.en: So they know about your solution.
sentences.zh: 他们知道你的解决方案了。

sentences.en: But they need proof objection handling testimonials and the rest.
sentences.zh: 但他们需要证据、异议处理、客户见证等等。

sentences.en: And then level five is most aware.
sentences.zh: 然后是第五级，“完全意识”。

sentences.en: So they simply haven't implemented it and need a little nudge over the edge.
sentences.zh: 他们只是还没行动，需要你轻轻推一把。

sentences.en: Now when I create these videos I always start by naming the problem. Literally.
sentences.zh: 我做这些视频的时候，总是从点明问题开始。毫不夸张。

sentences.en: Go back to the very start of this video.
sentences.zh: 你倒回去看这个视频的最开头。

sentences.en: What do I say?
sentences.zh: 我说了什么？

sentences.en: Nobody knows what skill to learn right now.
sentences.zh: 现在没人知道该学什么技能。

sentences.en: And what this does is it allows people to self qualify.
sentences.zh: 这句话的作用是让人们自我筛选。

sentences.en: Like do I know what skill to learn or do I not know what skill to learn?
sentences.zh: 比如，我知道该学什么技能吗？还是我不知道？

sentences.en: And it's also the start of the story, because when you start a story like a novel, you're usually in this place of tension and then it slowly gets resolved and then they go on an adventure and then they reach the conclusion.
sentences.zh: 这也是故事的开始，因为当你开始一个故事，比如一本小说，你通常就处在这种张力之中，然后张力慢慢化解，主角踏上冒险，最后到达结局。

sentences.en: So the best way to actually learn this is to just look and notice it on social media.
sentences.zh: 所以真正学会这个的最好方法，就是去社交媒体上观察和留意。

sentences.en: When people make a post, I guarantee that most of the posts you read have a problem that's implied or just directly stated.
sentences.zh: 当人们发帖时，我保证你读到的大多数帖子，都有一个隐含或直接说出来的问题。

sentences.en: This is the most powerful thing you can do.
sentences.zh: 这是你能做的最有力的事。

sentences.en: It's so simple.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: But just start with the problem in your writing speaking posts.
sentences.zh: 从你的写作、演讲、帖子里提出的问题开始。

sentences.en: At the start of your product, you need to frame the situation.
sentences.zh: 在你的产品开头，你需要先框定现状。

sentences.en: When you're trying to convince your wife that you want to go and have a night out with the boys, you start with a problem first and that will open them up much more to hearing your solution, which in your case is going out with the boys.
sentences.zh: 当你想说服你老婆，让你跟兄弟们出去嗨一晚，你得先抛出一个问题，这样她们会更愿意听你的解决方案——对你来说，就是跟兄弟们出去。

sentences.en: The problem could be all.
sentences.zh: 这个问题可以是，好吧。

sentences.en: You haven't had a night to yourself in a long time.
sentences.zh: 你已经很久没有属于自己的夜晚了。

sentences.en: You want to watch Gray's Anatomy and you can just have a chill night alone.
sentences.zh: 你想看《实习医生格蕾》，你只想一个人安安静静待一晚。

sentences.en: And then you continue on with the persuasive argument that you're making.
sentences.zh: 然后你再继续推进你正在构建的说服论证。

sentences.en: Now, another practice you can do here is to just name five problems you've experienced in your life. Seriously.
sentences.zh: 现在，另一个你可以做的练习是，列出你人生中经历过的五个问题。说真的。

sentences.en: Do that.
sentences.zh: 去做。

sentences.en: Think of the problems that you've experienced and boom, now you have five content ideas that you can go and post, and they're going to be a lot better than if you just thought of them from scratch.
sentences.zh: 想想你经历过的那些问题，砰，现在你就有五个内容创意可以拿去发了，而且它们会比凭空想出来的好得多。

sentences.en: And towards the end I'll mention it, but I actually created a prompt that acts as like a persuasion coach slash teacher slash writer.
sentences.zh: 在接近结尾的时候我会提到，但我实际上创建了一个提示词，它就像一个说服教练/老师/写手。

sentences.en: So if you just run the prompt, it'll ask you what you want, and you can practice with the prompt, and it'll help teach you human nature and persuasion a lot faster.
sentences.zh: 所以只要你运行这个提示词，它会问你想要什么，你可以用它来练习，它会帮你更快地学会人性和说服。

sentences.en: So the second psychological lever is mirror the identity, which aligns with the identity tension because you identify with a group or tribe without realizing it, like being a morning person or being a coffee drinker, or being a Christian, atheist, Republican, Democrat, anti-air, pro AI, or any of the other ideologies or religions we like to adopt as a part of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 第二个心理杠杆是镜像身份，这与身份张力一致，因为你会不自觉地认同某个群体或部落，比如做一个早起的人、一个喝咖啡的人，或者做一个基督徒、无神论者、共和党人、民主党人、反AI、支持AI，或者任何我们喜欢将其作为自身一部分的意识形态或宗教。

sentences.en: Now, as an example, here's a YouTube video that got 3.9 million views and the title is You're Not Forgetful My system for Memorizing everything.
sentences.zh: 现在，举个例子，这是一个获得390万次观看的YouTube视频，标题是《你不是健忘：我记住一切的系统》。

sentences.en: So it quite literally packages everything we've discussed into eight words problem, identity, solution.
sentences.zh: 所以它几乎把我们讨论的一切都打包进了八个字：问题、身份、解决方案。

sentences.en: And there are so many different ways to pull the identity lever.
sentences.zh: 而撬动身份杠杆的方式有无数种。

sentences.en: But my favorite way in the one that I go to is I just start with if you are or if you're and that's it.
sentences.zh: 但我最喜欢也最常用的方式，就是直接用“如果你是”或“如果你”开头，就这样。

sentences.en: If you're lazy, if you're broke, if you're unhappy, if you're a writer that hits the problem tension or the survival tension and the identity tension in one lever that you can pull, and all of those if you're lazy, if you're broke, if you're unhappy.
sentences.zh: 如果你懒，如果你穷，如果你不快乐，如果你是一个写作者，这在一个杠杆里同时击中了问题张力或生存张力，以及身份张力，所有这些：如果你懒，如果你穷，如果你不快乐。

sentences.en: They're the start of four almost viral social posts, or the start of a public speaking gig, or the start or title of a YouTube video.
sentences.zh: 它们是四个几乎注定会病毒式传播的社交帖子的开头，或者一场公开演讲的开头，或者一个YouTube视频的开头或标题。

sentences.en: And by the way, if you have interests or skills or knowledge that people already talk about online, I'll teach you my system for building an audience in a personal brand and writing compelling content that you actually resonate with in the content bootcamp that starts in five days.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你有别人已经在网上讨论的兴趣、技能或知识，我会在五天后开始的内容训练营里，教你建立受众和个人品牌的系统，以及撰写你真正有共鸣的、引人入胜的内容。

sentences.en: So link in the description I would enroll before then.
sentences.zh: 链接在描述栏，我建议在那之前报名。

sentences.en: I'll teach you my system for building an audience, a personal brand, and writing compelling content that you actually want to post and write about your interest in the content bootcamp, and that starts in a few days.
sentences.zh: 我会在内容训练营里教你建立受众、个人品牌，以及撰写你真正想发布、想写的、关于你兴趣的引人入胜的内容的系统，训练营几天后开始。

sentences.en: I don't know exactly when, because I don't know when this video is going out, but I would encourage enrolling before then.
sentences.zh: 我不知道确切时间，因为我不知道这个视频什么时候发出去，但我鼓励你在那之前报名。

sentences.en: Now, the third psychological lever is to exclude people and this is the identity tension deepened.
sentences.zh: 现在，第三个心理杠杆是排除他人，这是身份张力的深化。

sentences.en: So here you just want to explicitly name who it is not for, because exclusion creates that sense of belonging and it pushes people to pick a side.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你只需要明确指出这不是为谁准备的，因为排除会创造归属感，并推动人们选择立场。

sentences.en: Now this is best done after you mirror the identity from step two, which draws a line filtering out the wrong people who weren't going to support you anyways.
sentences.zh: 这最好在你完成第二步的镜像身份之后进行，它会划出一条线，过滤掉那些本来就不会支持你的错误人群。

sentences.en: So a few examples.
sentences.zh: 举几个例子。

sentences.en: And you've probably heard something like this before, but this isn't for people who want to try to get in shape.
sentences.zh: 你可能以前听过类似的话，但这不是给那些想“试着”健身的人准备的。

sentences.en: This is for people tired of their own excuses and ready to completely change their life.
sentences.zh: 这是给那些厌倦了自己的借口、准备好彻底改变人生的人准备的。

sentences.en: Example two if you're looking for a productivity hack or morning routine, you're in the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 例子二：如果你在寻找一个生产力技巧或晨间流程，你来错地方了。

sentences.en: Example three this isn't for people who want a dinky side hustle.
sentences.zh: 例子三：这不是给那些想搞个微不足道的副业的人准备的。

sentences.en: We're building a real business here, so I think you get that.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里建立的是真正的事业，我想你明白了。

sentences.en: And it leads to psychological lever number four, which is paint the transformation.
sentences.zh: 而这引出了第四个心理杠杆，描绘转变。

sentences.en: And this aligns with the progress tension.
sentences.zh: 而这正好与进度张力相呼应。

sentences.en: So essentially mastering human nature is about changing people's lives for the better, hopefully because that's how you build your life's work.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，掌握人性就是去改善他人的生活，希望如此，因为这就是你构建一生事业的方式。

sentences.en: You become a massive value creator.
sentences.zh: 你会成为一个巨大的价值创造者。

sentences.en: And this is how you create value for other humans, or at least something that's perceived as valuable.
sentences.zh: 这就是你为他人创造价值的方式，或者至少是创造某种被感知为有价值的东西。

sentences.en: You hone in on a purpose, and that purpose revolves around solving a problem for as many people as you can.
sentences.zh: 你聚焦于一个目标，这个目标的核心就是为尽可能多的人解决一个问题。

sentences.en: Persuasion is simply how you get people on board with that.
sentences.zh: 说服，只是你让人们认同这件事的方式。

sentences.en: So, so far, we've captured attention by naming the threat and filtered out those who don't match by mirroring the identity.
sentences.zh: 那么，到目前为止，我们通过指出威胁来抓住注意力，又通过镜像身份过滤掉了不匹配的人。

sentences.en: And now we create desire by simulating the future.
sentences.zh: 现在我们通过模拟未来来创造渴望。

sentences.en: So again, you can probably see at the beginning the introduction of this video, I hit all of these in a short amount of time.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经看出来了，在这个视频的开头介绍部分，我在很短的时间内就用上了所有这些技巧。

sentences.en: It was like three minutes.
sentences.zh: 大概就三分钟。

sentences.en: And so why does this work?
sentences.zh: 那么这为什么会奏效？

sentences.en: Well, one the problem catches attention.
sentences.zh: 首先，问题抓住了注意力。

sentences.en: And then the solution or the desired outcome or the end of the transformation causes you to actually experience the feeling of having that thing.
sentences.zh: 然后，解决方案、理想结果或转变的终点，会让你真正体验到拥有那件事物的感觉。

sentences.en: That's what the mind or the brain does.
sentences.zh: 这就是大脑的运作方式。

sentences.en: The same neural circuitry fires when you imagine an experience as when you actually have it. They're the same.
sentences.zh: 当你想象一种体验时，激活的神经回路和你真正拥有它时是一样的。完全一样。

sentences.en: Now, again, if this doesn't sound too practical, even though it's very practical, it's just hard to do unless you have something to apply it to.
sentences.zh: 重申一下，如果这听起来不够实用，尽管它非常实用，只是很难操作，除非你有可以应用它的载体。

sentences.en: So if you aren't posting on social media or giving public talks, or trying to get a promotion and trying to persuade your boss, you need a vessel to practice this, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你没有在社交媒体上发帖、做公开演讲，或者试图争取晋升、说服你的老板，你就需要一个容器来练习这个，对吧？

sentences.en: And in most jobs, you aren't in the position to do that because you don't have the direct feedback from reality.
sentences.zh: 而在大多数工作中，你并没有这样的机会，因为你得不到来自现实的直接反馈。

sentences.en: You aren't an entrepreneur, so if you want a way to practice it right now, again, I have the prompt link in the description.
sentences.zh: 你不是创业者，所以如果你想立刻找到练习的方法，再说一次，我在描述里放了提示词链接。

sentences.en: You just pop that into AI and then it can be your coach or your teacher or any of those things, and it will guide you through it.
sentences.zh: 你把它丢进 AI，它就可以成为你的教练、老师或任何这类角色，并引导你完成整个过程。

sentences.en: And you can use that while writing posts or newsletters or scripts or while you're preparing for a talk.
sentences.zh: 你可以在写帖子、写 newsletter、写脚本，或者准备演讲时使用它。

sentences.en: Really, anything while you're writing a book.
sentences.zh: 真的，任何场景都行，包括写书的时候。

sentences.en: And I think it's pretty dang cool and helpful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的非常酷，也非常有用。

sentences.en: Now, psychological lever number five is to just give the first step.
sentences.zh: 现在，第五个心理杠杆就是给出第一步。

sentences.en: And now this is the progress tension activated to an extent, because the reason most people don't change is because they don't believe they can actually do the thing.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上激活了进度张力，因为大多数人之所以不改变，是因为他们不相信自己真的能做到那件事。

sentences.en: They don't have clarity.
sentences.zh: 他们缺乏清晰度。

sentences.en: The comfort of their current life is more desirable than the discomfort of doing what it takes to solve the problem you're offering them a solution to.
sentences.zh: 他们当前生活的舒适，比解决你提供方案的那个问题所需的痛苦，更令人向往。

sentences.en: So in a tweet, this looks like don't overhaul your life overnight.
sentences.zh: 所以放在一条推特里，这就像：别试图一夜之间颠覆你的生活。

sentences.en: Just go to bed an hour earlier.
sentences.zh: 只要提前一小时上床睡觉就行。

sentences.en: So in a product, this looks like making the first step so stupidly simple that they just can't avoid getting results.
sentences.zh: 放在一个产品里，这就像把第一步设计得极其简单，简单到他们不可能得不到结果。

sentences.en: That's what makes your product valuable to them is time to result in.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的产品对他们有价值的地方：获得结果所需的时间。

sentences.en: Another interesting reason why this is just so powerful is that it causes the effect to kick in, which is that the brain hates uncompleted tasks.
sentences.zh: 这个技巧如此强大的另一个有趣原因是，它会触发一种效应，那就是大脑讨厌未完成的任务。

sentences.en: So once someone starts something or think about starting something, they can't help but complete it.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦有人开始做某件事，或者开始考虑做某件事，他们就会忍不住去完成它。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: The more you practice this, the more you practice human nature, the more it impacts every other skill that you acquire.
sentences.zh: 你越练习这个，越练习人性，它就越会影响你获得的每一项其他技能。

sentences.en: And when people or you go and learn the latest high value skills, essentially if it's a good skill, you're just learning a lower layer of human nature.
sentences.zh: 当人们或者你自己去学最新的高价值技能时，本质上，如果那是个好技能，你只是在学人性更底层的某一层。

sentences.en: So if you learn the meta skill itself, in practice, all of this, practice everything from that frame or from that lens, you can pick up almost any high value skill and do it better than everyone else, because the skills are going to continue to evolve.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你学了元技能本身，在实践中，用那个框架或那个视角去练习一切，你几乎可以掌握任何高价值技能，并且做得比所有人都好，因为技能会持续进化。

sentences.en: There's going to be new skills every single year that you're going to have to keep up with.
sentences.zh: 每年都会有新技能冒出来，你必须跟上。

sentences.en: And this is how you actually learn those faster and become valuable at them.
sentences.zh: 而这就是你真正更快学会它们、并变得有价值的方式。

sentences.en: Because, again, the people who have the money that you want to support your work and the opportunities and the resources are humans, so you need to study them.
sentences.zh: 因为，再说一次，那些拥有你想要的金钱来支持你工作、以及机会和资源的人，是人，所以你需要研究他们。

sentences.en: So that is it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Thank you for watching.
sentences.zh: 感谢观看。

sentences.en: If you want to start a personal brand, build an audience.
sentences.zh: 如果你想开启个人品牌，建立受众。

sentences.en: Learn how to write compelling content in your own voice and find your unique voice.
sentences.zh: 学会如何用自己的声音写出有吸引力的内容，找到你独特的声音。

sentences.en: The link to the content bootcamp is in the description that starts in a few days.
sentences.zh: 内容训练营的链接在简介里，几天后开营。

sentences.en: There's also the prompt in the description and a few other things that you might like, so check those out, like and subscribe before you leave.
sentences.zh: 简介里还有那个提示词和其他一些你可能喜欢的东西，离开前记得去看看、点赞和订阅。

sentences.en: Thank you for watching by.
sentences.zh: 感谢观看，再见。
